core_meaning.short_meaning: Concealer of faults; a divine name in traditional Islamic lists
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Sattar (الستار) is a divine name understood as “the Concealer” or “the One who covers faults”. It is transmitted in traditional lists of God's names rather than as a verbatim Qur'anic form. The root س ت ر means to cover or conceal, and Sattar and the compound Abd al-Sattar are common male names in South Asia and the Middle East.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root س ت ر gives satara (“to cover”) and sitr (“covering, concealment”). Traditional lists of the divine names include الستار, and a well-known report says that God is “Sattīr” (concealing). Because the form is not verbatim in the Qur'an, the record labels it as a traditional divine name rather than a Qur'anic one.
